Early-stopping greedy prefix matching on validated text: the actual longest_valid_prefix scan stops as soon as the derivative is the empty expression, since no longer prefix can then match. Its dead-state test is exact, and on every suffix with a UTF-8 decoding it returns exactly the result of the full longest_prefix scan, so every longest_prefix theorem applies to it. Text that is not valid UTF-8 keeps the full scan's diagnostics only through that full scan; this variant is used after whole-source validation. Fast Functional Syntax token selection on validated text: the lexer selects each token with the early-stopping matchers (longest_valid, next_terminal_valid) and runs only the matchers of terminals whose words can begin with the next code point (next_terminal_fast). The dispatch test is proved sound against the independent terminal languages: every word of every terminal begins with a code point that passes it, so a skipped terminal has no candidate endpoint and reports no match. On every suffix with a UTF-8 decoding both shortcuts are proved equal to the standard greatest selection next_terminal, and the stream proofs use those equalities, so the lexer's correctness theorems are unchanged. Compiled regular grammars: compile turns an expression into a table of nodes whose parts come before them, and the matcher runs partial derivatives over continuation stacks of node indices, so no part of the grammar is copied while matching. An independent reading of the table gives every node a language (a part that does not come before its node, and an index outside the table, read as the empty language); compiling keeps every node's empty-word flag equal to whether its language has the empty word and gives the root the expression's language. Each matching step is proved to replace the state's language by the words that remain after the consumed code point, so matches returns exactly the derivative matcher's matches_utf8 result, including malformed UTF-8 diagnostics, and on a suffix with a UTF-8 decoding longest_valid returns exactly longest_prefix's result. A table or state that would exceed the usize range is reported as None, and validate_iri and validate_reference then answer with the derivative matcher; their statements are unchanged. The prepared SHI queries of shi_ontology use the base whenever it fits.
